points.description: Correctly contrasts the two modes: asynchronous sends each character as a self-contained unit with start and stop bits (simple/cheap, low transmission rate), whereas synchronous groups many characters into a continuous stream/frames delimited by SYN or flag (more complex, higher transmission rate). Equivalent wording accepted.
points.partial_credit: Award half if only one mode is described correctly or the contrast is given without the key distinguishing feature (start/stop bits per character vs. frames of grouped characters).

rubric.notes: Full mark for a correct contrast: per-character start/stop bits (low rate) versus framed blocks of characters (higher rate). Half for describing only one mode correctly or a vague contrast. No marks for incorrect or irrelevant answers.
